item.title: Re: (Still) Awaiting Greenlight / The Book of the Sinners
item.content:encoded:
If it is really a bad idea, I could work out some sort of "punishment" or "bad thing" that would happen if within a certain time span no person chooses out of their own free will to take part in the trial.

This doesn't make it better: the issue is that the book is compelling itself to be used rather than there like…being a reason for the foundation to choose to use it. You're just, abstracting the force of the choice from 'the book gives literally no choice' to 'the book gives effectively no choice' since like, you have to use it to avoid the punishment/bad thing.

I really intend to make the tests as impactful and individual as possible. So there is an individual trial for each person with no reoccurring tests from past participants. I plan to make it a big emotional arc with character growth.

What are the tests? How are they impactful? What's the big emotional arc with character growth? How does one test flow to the next in the narrative here?

item.title: Re: (Still) Awaiting Greenlight / The Book of the Sinners
item.content:encoded:
About the first point:

Since this SCP is designed to "save humanity" from sinful volks within before the corruption is too advanced, it would make sense for the book to simply "force" a challenger. If it is really a bad idea, I could work out some sort of "punishment" or "bad thing" that would happen if within a certain time span no person chooses out of their own free will to take part in the trial.

About the second point:

I really intend to make the tests as impactful and individual as possible. So there is an individual trial for each person with no reoccurring tests from past participants. I plan to make it a big emotional arc with character growth.

Now the price at the end is a bit…I say even a mystery to myself because originally I planned to make a reference to SCP 001 "The Gate Guardian" but I am not sure if I am allowed to do so since I am a newbie and with SCP 001 being a big deal to make references to.

item.title: Re: (Still) Awaiting Greenlight / The Book of the Sinners
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

If no human voluntarily tests themselves within a day, the book will choose a sinful challenger within a certain radius around it.

This is generally a bad idea: forcing someone to use a scp is generally a lot less impactful than exploring what happens when someone chooses to use it.

Each of the two will give a unique perspective about the realm of the sins, the sins themselves (so to say their representatives), the seven tests, and the ones who failed the trial.

This feels like the meat of the article and my biggest issue is that I still don't have a good idea of what this is going to be like. Or, rather, my concern is that it feels very passive: there's no like, driving force here where we're invested in the outcome of this because there's no stakes to it? It doesn't really matter to use whether they succeed or not because it doesn't really change much. It could work without stakes if the actual tests are interesting, or with good characterisation of the researchers and like, a big emotional arc where they really grow over the course of the testing, but I'm not really sure what your plans are in regard to that?

You mention there's a prize if someone passes all the tests: this could be the thing that provides stakes but like, it really depends on what it is? If it's big enough, the Foundation might feel justified in throwing some d-class at this to try to get the prize, and that might get around the first issue I raised.

item.title: Re: (Still) Awaiting Greenlight / The Book of the Sinners
item.content:encoded:
I'm not exactly sure how the central narrative ties into the core anomaly: I assume that it means that while the book can kill anyone who reads it, it doesn't always choose to do so?

Beyond this, I'm not exactly sure what the central narrative is about, if you catch my drift: there's vague allusions to the individuals maybe knowing each other, and there being trials they face, but like…where does it all go? What's the big hook that like, engages a reader into caring about these people and the outcome of their trials? What actually happens during the trials? What are their characters and morals like?

My concern is that the outcome of this (both the characters dying) feels very obviously like it's going to happen: the description will almost certainly setup the lethality of this (if the ConProcs don't), and so it feels like the overall arc will be very obvious and then hard to get a reader to engage? I also feel like a generic item which judges the sins of someone is…not hugely interesting alone: it's something which is proposed a lot and almost never goes anywhere because it's just, not very interesting on it's own.

item.title: Re: Awaiting Greenlight / The Book of the Siners
item.content:encoded:
Hmmmm the problem I had before and the problem I have with a lot of first timers is that they end up giving a vague summary of/or a vague series of events and call it a narrative. While your updated pitch certainly is significantly improved, it still falls under very vague and not developed.

Maybe I can think of an example to help show you. Since you're doing something very biblical, I'll use God's creation of Adam and Eve as an example.

+I'll just add this example...
-Yeet

Imagine if the Garden of Eden and the creation of Adam and Eve and existence was someone's pitch. A lot of newbies would make something like this:

  • Powerful being creates everything

I'd ask for expansion and they'd do something along the lines of:

  • Powerful being makes universe, makes a garden and puts life in garden

When I want in-depth expansion. Not just a short summary replaced with a different, slightly more focused short vague summary.

What I want is:

  • An omnipotent, powerful being takes seven days to create all forms of life and locates them in the Garden of Eden. He creates Adam and allows him to enjoy the garden. He then creates Eve to be his companion. One day, a snake tempts them with the fruit of knowledge and God casts them out of the Garden, starting off the human race as we know it.

See what I mean? All three kinda mean the same thing (God creates everything) but the third one is the most interesting.

Your current one falls in a weird area slightly past the second example I have and way short of the third. I understand my example definitely isn't a perfect example, but I hope I helped elaborate on what I was looking for.

Now, I know this may disappoint, but I almost always only take two looks at any concept or draft. I'll be declining to return any more now. You can seek out other reviewers via the butterfly squad roster. They're really good people, so don't be shy now. If any of them don't respond in a few days, you can always send followup PMs as long as you're not spamming them. Keep in mind if a reviewer is in high demand and has a busy personal life, there's a possibility they can gloss over you by mistake. They're not ignoring you, they're just busy people. Don't sweat it.

You're definitely getting there, so don't give up! The greenlight process can be a challenging one, but the end result is well, well worth it. Have a good day, partner.

P.S. I'm not exactly a high demand reviewer, so thank you for reaching out to me and considering me 👍 it felt nice

item.title: Re: Awaiting Greenlight / The Book of the Siners
item.content:encoded:
+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

I think I can very quickly summarize this as, 'generic biblical-themed pay-for-your-sins anomalous punishment object.' It falls into the Series 1 trope of being a thing that does a thing and exists for seemingly no reason other than what it is.

The Central Narrative is a very long extension of the Elevator Pitch, which is where the anomalous description is supposed to go. Because of this, this SCP essentially has no story.

I'm very much fascinated by religious and spiritual imagery and themes as well as the psychological aspect of it all. The idea of an SCP that makes people own up to their sins or get #rekt otherwise is some that innately appeals to me, as it portrays humanity in its purest, rawest form. However, this is as generic as generic gets. It might as well be God descending on random people and telling them to git gud or git fucked.

Apologies if this was harsh. To be fair, the anomaly works. It's kinda bland, but almost any anomaly can work nowadays if you attach a good enough story to it.

Tell you what. Here's a suggestion. You know what would make this work? Showing us someone going through its trials and tribulations. Considering how character-focused this anomaly innately needs to be, make a character(s), flesh them out, and have them undergo its trials. Forget test logs. This thing doesn't need them. One or two people will be enough to show off its obvious effects.

Show us someone at their lowest low before they come up. Or, ya know, having then go even further down. I think two characters would be best for this since you'd want to show us the good path and the bad path.

Anywho, I hope I helped and I bid you a good day. 👍

item.title: Awaiting Greenlight / The Book of the Sinners
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlight: Yes

Page type: SCP Article

Elevator pitch: To save humanity from corruption and wickedness of itself, the seven deadly sins, guidance for humans, were created. However, one individual or entity managed to manifest the sins in our realm inside a book. The ultimate way to cleanse pure humans and irradicate the sinners from corrupting the rest. Anyone willing to read from the book of sinners shall be tested by the sins itself of their purity and corruptness. Those unlucky to fail will have their soul trapped inside the book, and their face, name, and sin burned on the last pages of the book, being held captive for all eternity. If no human voluntarily tests themselves within a day, the book will choose a sinful challenger within a certain radius around it. Unfortunately, to this date, there is no record of anyone passing all the seven sins successfully. The corruption of sins must have spread out of control because a corrupt mind will corrupt its kind.

Central narrative: The main focus will be around two site researchers assigned to this anomaly. Both will get themselves challenged by the sins, with one successfully passing it. The first one being forced by the book to read the first page because within a day, no volunteer was found. The other voluntarily trapping herself inside the book to prevent another human from being randomly selected. Each of the two will give a unique perspective about the realm of the sins, the sins themselves (so to say their representatives), the seven tests, and the ones who failed the trial.
One or two short test logs might be added to demonstrate certain "incidents" regarding this SCP. For example, a researcher is forced by the book to read the first page, after he forced a child to do the same.

Hook, attention grabber: Interesting to me is to learn about the different trial runs of the two individuals with their backstory, moral thoughts, and purest form.
Add to that the few hints around the price, or let's call it achievement someone would receive if he or she passes all the tests.
